newsitem.title: USA: Box Church boosts St. Mary reserves.
newsitem.headline: Box Church boosts St. Mary reserves.

text.p: St. Mary Land & Exploration Co said Wednesday the Box Church Field in East Texas added 26.4 billion cubic feet of natural gas to the company's reserves.

The proved reserves from Box Church "are equal to 35 percent of our total company proved gas reserves as of December 31, 1995," St. Mary said, adding the Box Church finding costs are less than $0.32 per thousand cubic feet.
Led by "the Box Church Field and significant drilling success in each of our core areas, we expect record production replacement in 1996," the company said.
St. Mary and its privately-owned partner acquired the Box Church Field (2,112 gross acres) in Limestone County, Texas, in four separate transactions during 1995 and 1996.
St. Mary said its net acquisition cost totaled $2.6 million, adding the company operates and holds an average 58 percent working interest in three units comprising the field.

When acquired, the field had existing production of about 3.3 million cubic feet daily from the deeper Smackover formation. However, the potential of the Travis Peak and Cotton Valley formations had not been recognized by the previous owners.
The use of improved formation evaluation and state of the art hydraulic fracturing techniques has enabled St. Mary to produce previously by-passed pays, it said.

This year, St. Mary said, its 60 percent owned discovery well, the Wilson 2, encountered 200 feet of net pay in the Upper and Lower Travis Peak and Cotton Valley formations, had six successful drill stem tests, and was completed in the Cotton Valley at 3.5 million cubic feet of natural gas daily with multiple productive zones behind pipe in the Travis Peak.

Subsequently, a confirmation well, the 57.49 percent owned White 2, was completed in the Cotton Valley at 2.7 million; and the 56.94 percent owned Keris 3 is cleaning up after completion at over 2.6 million from the Cotton Valley.

St. Mary said it expects to produce the well as a dual Cotton Valley - Travis Peak completion. A fourth well, the 57.49 percent owned White 5 is currently drilling at a twin location to the White 2 and will be dually completed in the Upper and Lower Travis Peak.

St. Mary's 1997-1998 development program at Box Church provides for an additional eight Cotton Valley wells and five Travis Peak wells to fully develop the proved reserves at an average completed well cost of about $850,000 per well.
St. Mary said it has arranged a long term rig contract and will drill about one well per month until the field is fully developed. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
